X.note: The water, terrain and hills are a decent low-poly 3D reveal, but the batteries are tiny dark slabs with weak smoke. The stacked captions cover the sky and the bay. The Gibraltar fortress and town are small and hard to make out. The leader line points at a single ship for no clear reason. Caption text is small for a phone, and the date chip is the only large text. One hull is clipped at the bottom right, behind the source bar. The 'positions illustrative' caveat weakens the visual claim.

Y.note: This is a dense, impressive photogrammetry-style city model with real lighting and a recognisable runway and harbour. It reads as a wide reveal of the whole place. The big number chip is very legible. The model has visible artifacts: smeared textures in the green areas, a hard cut-off edge along the water, and flat blue water. The attribution bar and the sub-caption are small on a phone. The huge amount of detail has no focal point, and the bottom attribution crowds the year chip.

why: Y shows a richer, more convincing whole-place reveal with a bold, instantly readable headline stat, while X's tiny ships and stacked small captions make it feel sparse and overlaid.
top_fix_for_weaker: Make the batteries much larger and more detailed, with visible gun ports and strong muzzle flashes and smoke. Pull the camera lower and closer to the line and the Rock. Merge the two caption boxes into one short headline of 28pt or larger, such as '10 floating batteries'. Move the source credit to a small footer, and keep every hull in frame.
